title: Carroll legislators call for Bouchat’s resignation
summary: Republican state lawmakers today called for the resignation of Del. Christopher Eric Bouchat (R-Frederick and Carroll) after press reports detailed his refusal to attend legislative sessions and committee meetings over the last month.
content:
by Bryan P. Sears, Maryland Matters March 25, 2026

by Bryan P. Sears, Maryland Matters March 25, 2026

Republican state lawmakers today called for the resignation of Del. Christopher Eric Bouchat (R-Frederick and Carroll) after press reports detailed his refusal to attend legislative sessions and committee meetings over the last month.

Maryland Matters reported last week that Bouchat was driving to Annapolis to register his presence and then immediately leaving to go to work. He sent a letter to House Speaker Joseline Peña-Melnyk attempting to resign his seat on the House Judiciary Committee and urged Republicans to resign their committee assignments.

On Wednesday, after a second report of Bouchat’s actions, Sen. Justin Ready and Dels. April Rose and Chris Tomlinson called for Bouchat to resign.

All three lawmakers represent the same District 5 as Bouchat, which includes Frederick and Carroll counties. Rose and Tomlinson sit in the back of the chamber next to Bouchat’s empty seat.

In their statement, the lawmakers wrote that they “are calling on him to resign from the General Assembly and allow a qualified replacement to be selected to fill the remainder of the term through January 2027.”

Bouchat, who is in the fourth year of his first term, did not file for re-election. He took his colleagues’ call in stride.

Bouchat, in bout of frustration, skipping floor votes and committee sessions as term ends

“I should treat them all to dinner,” Bouchat said in an email. “They are my friends and I love them. ”

So far, leaders of the House Republican Caucus have stopped short of calling for resignation or removal.

House Minority Leader Del. Jason C. Buckel (R-Allegany) said he was aware of the call for Bouchat to resign.

“I respect their viewpoint,” Buckel said in a text. “I hope that Delegate Bouchat reconsiders his stance and fully participates in the General Assembly over the last few weeks of this session and fulfills his responsibilities throughout his term if he chooses to continue in office and receive compensation therefore.”

In a series of emails to Maryland Matters last week, Bouchat detailed his frustration with Annapolis, where Republicans are a minority. He also complained that the job has cost him financially, citing more than $200,000 in losses.

Bouchat’s District 5 colleagues said that calling on “a duly elected legislator to resign is not something we take lightly but Delegate Bouchat has apparently been engaging in this pattern since the end of February.”

“In that time he has missed key votes on energy, public safety, education, protecting children and much more,” their statement said. “He has engaged in odd and counterproductive behavior off and on for the entire term but this latest pronouncement that his participation in the Maryland General Assembly has ended deprives the citizens of District 5 the full representation they deserve. Even more offensively, Delegate Bouchat seems to be asking them to keep paying his salary despite not staying around to actually do the job.”

On Wednesday, the House was scheduled to take up a floor debate on the budget as amended by the House Appropriations Committee.

Bouchat, as he has for the last month, came to the chamber and registered his presence. Following the opening prayer, he left. On his way out, he exchanged pleasantries with a reporter.

The statement was released after Bouchat left.

“I face to face thanked Delegate Tomlinson for informing me of the delegation move and expressed my love for him,” Bouchat said in a second email to a reporter. “This is all going exquisitely well. The 2030 Governor election will be decided by swing voters not Republicans and this is solidifying it.”

“Now the public can hear a debate about how the insiders want to pick my replacement and their motive is not having someone vote, since there is no time to do so, but hand pick and guarantee who they want. Soon the session ends and I am far more capable of fulfilling the interim duties than a replacement lacking influence and experience,” he continued. “It is up to the public to elect the next Delegate with all the candidates equal. If I resign that fairness ends and what the public does not like will rule; Insiders deciding.”

The three lawmakers Wednesday said his absence hurts his constituents and the public perception of elected officials.

“Following press reports and Delegate Bouchat’s confirmation that he has ‘resigned from his committee’ and has only been attending session in the morning to record his presence before then leaving Annapolis to run his business,  We and all the residents of District 5 voted for three Delegates to represent our interests and concerns for the full four-year term,” the three wrote in a statement.

“The job of state legislators does not end with the conclusion of session in April. There is work all through the year to address citizen concerns and participate in community events and discussions,” they wrote. “For these reasons, Delegate Bouchat should resign so that a qualified person can be chosen to provide representation during the interim until the start of the new term in January.”

By law, the House and the Senate are responsible for setting the rules for their respective chambers. A portion of the Maryland Constitution allows for lawmakers to be removed for “failure to act” — a provision that has never been invoked.
